caption: Figure 1: SBERT architecture with classification objective function, e.g., for fine-tuning on SNLI dataset. The two BERT networks have tied weights (siamese network structure).
description:
This figure is a diagram showing the architecture of Sentence-BERT (SBERT) with a classification objective function. It depicts two BERT networks with tied weights, forming a siamese network structure. The input sentences, A and B, are processed by separate BERT networks, followed by pooling layers. The pooled outputs are then combined and fed into a softmax classifier.

Text in figure: "Softmax classifier", "(u, v, |u-v|)", "u", "pooling", "BERT", "Sentence A", "v", "pooling", "BERT", "Sentence B".

Description: The architecture consists of two BERT networks processing sentences A and B, respectively. Each BERT network is followed by a pooling layer. The pooled outputs from both networks are combined and input into a softmax classifier.

caption: Figure 2: SBERT architecture at inference, for example, to compute similarity scores. This architecture is also used with the regression objective function.
description:
This figure is a diagram showing the architecture of Sentence-BERT (SBERT) for computing similarity scores between sentences. It illustrates the process of transforming two sentences, A and B, into embeddings using BERT, pooling these embeddings, and then calculating the cosine similarity between them. The diagram includes the following components: two input sentences, BERT embeddings, pooling layers, and a cosine similarity function. The output is a similarity score ranging from -1 to 1.

Text in figure: cosine-sim(u, v), u, pooling, BERT, Sentence A, v, pooling, BERT, Sentence B, -1...1
